item.title: New York Mayor Mamdani says companies like Netflix will now pay if you can't cancel
item.description: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's Click-to-Cancel rule is now in effect, requiring businesses to let customers cancel subscriptions the same way they signed up. Enforced by the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, it covers streaming services like Netflix, Amazon Prime and Disney+, as well as gym memberships. Violations carry civil penalties starting at $525 and possible refunds. New Yorkers can file complaints through a new online city portal.

item.title: New York fire fundraiser topped $100,000; state AG seeks $71,539 in unpaid funds
item.description: Hailey Bodah, a young New Yorker, faced unimaginable loss when a fire claimed the lives of her father and four sisters. In the wake of this tragedy, generous relatives raised over $100,000 to help her. However, legal issues emerged regarding the management of the funds, with the New York Attorney General’s office demanding the return of over $71,000.

item.title: Taylor Swift’s $4m Nashville education centre now showcases local student art
item.description: In 2012, Taylor Swift donated $4 million to create an education center at the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum. This center focuses on engaging children and families with the history of country music. Currently, it hosts an exhibition called Connection featuring works by students and artists from Friends Life Community. Participants learn letterpress printing techniques and create their own unique posters.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Jackie Chan and fans raised over $192,000 to help build schools in rural China
item.description: Jackie Chan transformed the act of giving into a global movement, urging fans to pitch in small donations for constructing schools in rural China. After six years, the initiative garnered over $96,000, which Chan generously matched, resulting in a remarkable total of over $192,000. This remarkable effort not only facilitated multiple school buildings but also underscored the power of collective action in uplifting communities through education.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Jeff Bezos invests $100 million to turn vacant land into parks in eight US cities
item.description: Jeff Bezos is allocating $100 million to convert neglected urban land into parks in eight American cities. The funding aims to revitalize vacant lots and industrial sites while enhancing community access to nature. Specific projects include restoring public spaces in Cleveland, creating parks in Indianapolis, and improving green areas in Salt Lake City. Cities such as Los Angeles and Little Rock will benefit from new recreational and gathering spaces.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Steve McQueen’s former Malibu home bought for $8.35m now lists for $16.995m
item.description: Steve McQueen's iconic Malibu beach house passed through several ownership hands before receiving significant renovations from its latest buyers. Boasting oceanfront decks and private beach access, this esteemed property is nestled within an exclusive gated community. Initially bought for $8.35 million, it was revamped and relisted at $16.995 million, eventually selling for $13.6 million in September 2023, with its connection to McQueen and MacGraw continuing to garner interest.

item.title: Travis Kelce warns NFL as Patrick Mahomes and Chiefs dominate in 2026
item.description: Travis Kelce sent a confident message to the NFL after the Kansas City Chiefs improved to 4-0 in the 2026 season. Sharing a photo with Patrick Mahomes and Xavier Worthy on Instagram Stories, Kelce wrote, “Just the beginning!!” Mahomes and running back Kenneth Walker III have powered the Chiefs' offence, while the team continues to strengthen its defence. Kansas City returns after its Week 5 bye to face the Los Angeles Chargers.

item.title: WWE Money in the Bank 2026: Confirmed matches, start time and how to watch
item.description: WWE Money in the Bank 2026 is set for October 10 at the Smoothie King Center in New Orleans. This thrilling event will showcase five confirmed matches, featuring top wrestlers and diverse match formats. Fans can anticipate an exhilarating title defense as Roman Reigns faces LA Knight first. To accommodate international viewers, various start times have been designated, while fans in the US can catch the live broadcast on ESPN.

item.title: How CJP’s 'Jantar Mantar 2.0' call outgrew its venue, spread across cities
item.description: Protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar occurred in multiple Indian cities over perceived electoral roll irregularities. In Delhi, over 7,000 people were detained while attempting to gather at Jantar Mantar. Similar protests took place in Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Ahmedabad, resulting in hundreds of detentions. Police cited safety and law-and-order concerns, leading to heavy barricading and police monitoring.
item.dc:creator: VRITI JAIN

item.title: US death row inmate Christa Pike back in prison from hospital after failed execution
item.description: Christa Pike, a Tennessee death row inmate, has returned to prison after a failed execution attempt. The September 30 incident resulted in her needing medical care after the lethal injection process failed. Governor Bill Lee has ordered a review of the state's execution procedures following this incident. Pike had been sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of her classmate, Colleen Slemmer.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: ‘Amitabh Bachchan is hero for us, but he’s allowed to be human’: Abhishek on his father
item.description: Amitabh Bachchan is celebrating his 84th birthday on October 11 with numerous wishes from admirers. On the occasion, here's recalling the time when Abhishek Bachchan shared insights about their family dynamics and his father's dual role as a star and family man. He also spoke about how his parents feel about his career and how seeing his father at home despite being a superstar, taught him to stay detach from fame early on in life.

item.title: ‘Where is he?’ CJP seeks Dipke’s release ahead of grandma’s last rites on Sunday
item.description: The Cockroach Janta Party is seeking the release of its leader Abhijeet Dipke following his detention by Delhi Police. Dipke's family wishes to speak with him before his grandmother's last rites, scheduled for Sunday morning. Despite police claims of informing him about his grandmother's death, CJP continues to question his current whereabouts. Additionally, CJP has called for the immediate release of all other detained leaders.
item.dc:creator: LAIRENLAKPAM WARLI

item.title: Landlord wanted tenant out for law office; Delhi HC rejects tenant's objections
item.description: Two landlords, who were practising advocates, said they needed the rented premises to set up a law office. The tenant argued that the landlords had changed their stated purpose for seeking possession and already had other properties that could be used for their professional work. The tenant opposed the eviction and applied for leave to defend.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: Couple with legs chained found dead in Tapi river, Dhule police suspect suicide
item.description: Shyam Patil and his wife Sapna were discovered dead in the Tapi river in Dhule. Their bodies were chained together, indicating a possible suicide after their last phone call. Local residents reported seeing a motorcycle parked near the river before the discovery. Shyam had contacted his brother-in-law shortly before their presumed drowning, stating that everything was over.
item.dc:creator: SANTOSH SONAWANE

item.title: Delhi protests: CJP stir against CEC triggers political face-off - top developments
item.description: Delhi Police detained upwards of 37000 demonstrators on Saturday, protesting against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter-list manipulation, insisting on his resignation. Prominent political figures such as Arvind Kejriwal and Mamata Banerjee were among those arrested. Opposition members criticized the government for suppressing free speech by halting protests and imposing internet shutdowns, while the BJP defended their stance, calling the demonstrations a ploy to incite chaos.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: Earthquake of magnitude 4.2 hits Uttarakhand's Uttarkashi
item.description: A 4.2-magnitude earthquake struck Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand, on Saturday night, with its epicentre around 2 km northwest of the district headquarters and a focal depth of 11 km.
item.dc:creator: ASHISH MISHRA

item.title: 'Ab jawaab bhi dena padega': CJP claims member ‘brutally assaulted’ by Delhi Police
item.description: Cockroach Janta Party claimed that its Mumbai lead, Pranay Ahire, was assaulted during a protest in Delhi. The party stated that he is currently receiving medical treatment in the hospital. CJP criticized the police's actions as a violation of democratic rights and vowed to challenge the incident. Additionally, other CJP leaders were detained by police ahead of the protest demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.

item.title: 'I think it should be taken out': Rahane joins calls to abolish Impact Player rule
item.description: Ajinkya Rahane has raised significant concerns regarding the Impact Player rule in the Indian Premier League. He argues that this rule stifles the development of all-rounders in Indian cricket, restricting their vital opportunities on the field. Although some teams have exploited this rule for higher scores, it diminishes the role of bowlers and all-rounders.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: Actor Imran Khan among several detained in Mumbai for supporting CJP protest
item.description: Actor Imran Khan was among many detained by Mumbai Police during a protest supporting the Cockroach Janata Party. Protesters gathered near Nana Chowk, leading to their detention as police restricted movement in the area. August Kranti Maidan, intended for the demonstration, was locked down and heavily guarded. Separate protests also occurred with Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi workers being detained at Hutatma Chowk.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Happy Shardiya Navratri 2026: Best wishes, quotes, messages
item.description: As Shardiya Navratri draws near, families nationwide are immersing themselves in the joy of nine festive nights. Temples gleam with decorations, garba spaces come alive, and heartfelt greetings ripple through communities. Messages of love and support are exchanged among friends and colleagues, highlighting unity and devotion. This season brings everyone together, reinstating cherished traditions and sharing blessings in vibrant, meaningful ways.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Rob Parker criticises undefeated Vikings as offense struggles to score touchdowns
item.description: The Minnesota Vikings are 4-0, but Rob Parker believes their poor offense makes them the NFL’s weakest unbeaten team. Two victories without an offensive touchdown have raised concerns, even as their defense and kicker Will Reichard keep delivering results. Minnesota now needs to improve its attack to prove its perfect start reflects genuine strength.

item.title: ‘He is somewhat similar to me’: Sehwag says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is in his prime
item.description: Virender Sehwag draws parallels between his explosive batting style and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's fearless gameplay. The 15-year-old prodigy has made waves in T20Is, showcasing an impressive strike rate and accumulating runs effortlessly. Sehwag emphasises that age should take a backseat to performance at higher levels of cricket, especially with seasoned competitors like Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma vying for opening positions.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH
